whole from `compare/exec-summary.md` and appends it as the last numbered
section, on its own landscape page.

**Do not re-type it into the run summary.** It is the only place in the report
where each competitor's own observed value sits beside ours, it is built from
four separate captures, and a hand-copied second version is how one number
comes to differ between two pages of one document.

**The `icp` lens's `## ICP profiles` section is lifted the same way** — `render_report.py`
finds the heading in `icp/exec-summary.md` and renders the three profiles, the
trap and the candidates table as the *Ideal Customer Profiles* section, whole.
Do not re-type a profile into the run summary; quote its name and role and
point at the section.

`## Against comparable sites` earlier in the summary stays, and stays short: it
carries our column and the lead/trail/level count, for the reader who stops
before the findings. The matrix at the end is the evidence behind it — summary
and detail, the same split as the Top 5 against the per-lens sections.

> Requested 2026-09-05 by the first client to read one: the summary told him
> where the site trailed but never showed what the other three actually did, so
> the comparison could not be checked. The lens had built the table; only the
> export was dropping it.

#### ⚑ The order is fixed, and the table announces it

`LENS_ORDER` in `render_report.py` — **Clarity · Conversion · Trust · Ideal
customer profiles · Compare · SEO · AEO · Technical**, then **Usability ·
Defects · Activation · Content** —
is the order the detailed sections appear in, the order the contents lists
them, and the order "What each check looked for" must use.

> Observed 2026-09-05: the summary's own table listed the checks in one order
> and the document presented them in another. A reader who uses the table as a
> map is then wrong on every jump, and the report looks assembled rather than
> written. **If you reorder the table, you have introduced a bug.**

**Check names are Title Case; `SEO` and `AEO` are always upper case.** They are
what the client reads, never the folder name.

| Folder | In the report |
|---|---|
| `clarity` | Clarity |
| `conversion` | Conversion |
| `trust` | Trust and credibility |
| `icp` | Ideal Customer Profiles |
| `compare` | Competitive comparison |
| `seo` | Search visibility |
| `aeo` | Answer-engine readiness |
| `technical` | Performance and delivery |
| `ux` | Usability |
| `bugs` | Defects |
| `onboarding` | Activation |
| `content` | Content |

`render_report.py` uses this same mapping (`LENS_LABELS`), so a report that says
"aeo" in one table and "Answer-engine readiness" in the next looks like two
documents stapled together.

is a relative path and stays one; the link *text* is the display name. A
sentence like "see `trust/findings-final.md` in the run folder" is meaningless
to someone who was sent a PDF — say "in the full report".

#### Ranking across lenses is legitimate — merging is not

`severity-rubric.md` is shared and lens-agnostic: P0–P3 are defined by user impact, not by lens, and every lens loads it. **So you may rank findings from different lenses against each other.** Note in the limits that scoring models differed if they did — the manifest records which.

**Do not rewrite, merge or re-score a lens's finding.** Quote its title, cite its ID, link to its report.

#### ⚑ Cross-lens corroboration — the one thing only this layer can see

Lens reports deliberately do not dedupe against each other (`report-template.md`): each stands alone. So the same problem legitimately appears in several. **At the run level, say so:**

> **[P0] Memories asserts facts that are not the user's** — flagged independently by `ux`, `bugs` and `onboarding`

**Three independent lenses reaching the same finding is the strongest signal this architecture can produce** — the lenses never read each other, so agreement is real corroboration rather than an echo. Reported as three separate findings it reads as padding; reported as a corroboration count it reads as confidence.

Rules: a corroborated finding takes **one** slot in the top 3, not three. Count lenses, never average severities — cite the highest and say which lens assigned it.

**`render_report.py` also computes this mechanically** and prints a "Raised by
more than one check" table above the lens sections, plus an *Also raised by*
note on each affected row. That is a floor, not a substitute: it pairs findings
on a shared verbatim quotation or a similar title at the same locator, so it
catches the obvious agreements and misses ones phrased differently. **Your
top-3 corroboration counts are the authoritative ones** — write them from
reading the lens reports, not from the generated table.

It never merges, re-scores or drops anything (§11.8) — a false pair costs a
misleading note, not a lost finding.

Some kind of notes app that syncs between devices — I'm going from the name and one line halfway down the page; the headline never said.

1	# Report template
2	
3	**[M] methodology.** **Pass 2 only.** Produces two files per lens in the run folder: `exec-summary.md` and `findings-final.md`.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## ⚑ House style — pyramid, bullets, no prose
8	
9	This applies to **every line of every file a lens writes**, not just the summary.
10	
11	1. **Conclusion first, everywhere.** The finding title *is* the conclusion. The exec summary opens with the verdict. A reader who stops after one line must still have the answer.
12	2. **Bullets, not paragraphs.** No prose blocks anywhere in a report. If a thought needs three sentences, it is three bullets — or it is two thoughts.
13	3. **One idea per bullet, ≤ 25 words.** Longer means it is really two bullets.
14	4. **Cut anything that does not change a decision.** Background, throat-clearing, "it is worth noting that", restating the framework. The reader knows why they ran this.
15	5. **Numbers over adjectives.** "2:41 to first value" beats "reasonably quick".
16	
17	**Why this is a rule and not a preference:** a lens can produce twenty findings, and a run can carry seven lenses. Prose does not survive that volume — it is skimmed, then skipped, then the report goes unread and the run was wasted. Pyramid structure is what lets a reader stop at any depth and still be correctly informed.
18	
19	**What concision must never cost:** evidence citations, repro steps, or the severity. Compress the *reasoning*, never the *proof*. A finding stripped of its evidence is not concise, it is unsupported — see `evidence-rules.md`.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Why the exec summary leads with a verdict
24	
25	The one-sentence verdict and the top-3 are the only things standing between the user and a great deal of unread output. **Phase-2 gate check 6 enforces this mechanically** — a report whose first non-heading block is not a single sentence fails the gate.
26	
27	Write the verdict first, before the findings. If you cannot state the verdict in one sentence, you have not finished analysing.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## `exec-summary.md` (per lens)
32	
33	**Length: about one page.** Soft target, not a gate — but every line past it should have earned its place.
34	
35	```markdown
36	# <Product> — <lens> — Run <YYYY-MM-DD> (<run-id>)
37	
38	<ONE SENTENCE. The strongest honest reading of the evidence. No hedging,
39	no "it depends", no list. This is the line someone repeats in a meeting.>
40	
41	## Top 3
42	1. **[P0] <Title>** — <one line: the cost, not the description> (<personas>)
43	2. **[P1] <Title>** — <one line> (<personas>)
44	3. **[P1] <Title>** — <one line> (<personas>)
45	
46	## Score
47	- **Score:** <N>/10 — <one line saying what drove it, in the reader's terms>
48	
49	## Limits on this read
50	- **Personas:** <list> — ⚠ INFERRED (generic) | researched (supplied)
51	- **Not reached:** <surfaces, flows — or "none">
52	- **Excluded:** <scope exclusions, verbatim — auth wall always>
53	- **Models:** traversal `<model>` · scoring `<model>`
54	
55	## Numbers
56	| Persona | TTFV | Reading | Self-explanatory | Promise match |
57	|---|---|---|---|---|
58	| <name> | <MM:SS> | healthy / at risk / not reached | Pass/Partial/Fail | Pass/Partial/Fail |
59	
60	## Severity flips
61	<One line per behaviour scoring differently across personas. "None" if none —
62	and if only one persona ran, say that instead: a flip could not be observed.>
63	
64	## Next action
65	<One line.>
66	```
67	
68	### ⚑ The score
69	
70	**You assign it, because you are the only one who read the evidence.** The run
71	report renders every lens's score in one table with an overall figure, so this
72	number is read by the client beside the other checks — a lens that scores
73	generously, or harshly, distorts every other lens's number by comparison.
74	
75	- **10** — nothing to fix that a reasonable reviewer would raise.
76	- **8–9** — works; the findings are polish.
77	- **6–7** — works, with friction a real user would notice and complain about.
78	- **4–5** — a user gets through, but a meaningful share would give up or distrust it.
79	- **2–3** — the job this check covers mostly fails.
80	- **0–1** — unusable on this dimension.
81	
82	**Gate check 7 refuses a score its own severities contradict** — above 5/10
83	carrying a P0, above 7/10 carrying a P1, above 9/10 carrying a P2. The ceiling
84	is loose on purpose: it stops a number nobody could defend, it does not
85	second-guess a judgement inside the band — and it is a ceiling, not a target.
86	**Score from what the personas did, then check the ceiling; never start from
87	the ceiling and subtract.** Every persona reached value and would return is a
88	6–7 even with a P1 and a dozen P2s; the 4–5 band means someone actually gave
89	up. The bands, with what each looks like, are in `lens-output-contract.md`.
90	Score the dimension, not the count of findings — eleven P3s is a tidy 8, not
91	a 3.
92	
93	**Never write the overall score.** It is the mean of the lens scores, computed
94	by `render_report.py`, so the cover and the table cannot disagree.
95	
96	**⚑ If `persona_mode` is `generic`, the inferred-persona warning appears in the summary itself, not a footnote.** Findings resting on personas the agent invented are materially weaker than findings from researched ones, and a reader who misses that will over-trust the report.
97	
98	---
99	
100	## `findings-final.md` (per lens)
101	
102	```markdown
103	# <Product> — <lens> findings — Run <YYYY-MM-DD> (<run-id>)
104	
105	## Method
106	- Framework: <the lens's framework, one line>
107	- Pass 1 naive capture → Pass 2 analyst scoring
108	- Personas: <generic — INFERRED | supplied — researched>
109	- Scoring model: <model>
110	- Every finding cites an artifact; unsupported observations dropped, listed at the end
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Findings
115	
116	> **⚑ This block is machine-parsed.** `check_report.py` reads it field by field
117	> and fails closed — a field it cannot find is treated as absent, and an absent
118	> `Flow` silently changes the finding's ID. **Keep every field on its own
119	> bullet; never merge them onto one line with `·` separators.** A `·` inside a
120	> field's value is fine and expected (several artifacts on one Evidence line);
121	> it is only the field bullets themselves that must stay separate.
122	>
123	> **The `<finding-id>` is computed, never composed** — see the lens agent's
124	> Output section for the `finding_id.py` invocation. Write the block first, then
125	> hash exactly the `flow`, `locator` and `title` strings you wrote.
126	
127	### <finding-id> — <The conclusion, in one line, dev-ticketable>
128	- **Severity:** P0 | P1 | P2 | P3
129	- **So what:** <ONE line. What this costs this persona. The reason to fix it.>
130	- **Framework tags:** <A?, B-G?, C-? — per the lens>
131	- **Flow:** <shape_1 | shape_2 | shape_2b | shape_3>
132	- **Locator:** <the exact string you passed to finding_id.py --locator>
133	- **Personas hit:** <comma-separated>
134	- **Observed:**
135	  - <bullet — neutral and concrete>
136	  - <bullet>
137	  - <max 3; if it needs a fourth it is probably two findings>
138	- **Evidence:** `persona-<slug>/screenshots/NN-*.png` · `session.log:NN`
139	  > "<verbatim persona quote, if there is one>"
140	- **Repro:**
141	  1. …
142	  2. …
143	- **Fix:** <One line. A direction, not a spec.>
144	```
145	
146	**⚑ `Fix` is client-facing.** It is not a note to yourself: `render_report.py`
147	prints it as a *Recommended fix* column beside every finding in the exported
148	report, so it is one of the four things a paying reader actually sees. Write it
149	as an instruction someone could hand to a developer or a copywriter — name the
150	surface and the change. *"Delete the eyebrow, and add a self-serve link from
151	that section to /restaurants"* is a fix; *"reconsider the framing"* is not.
152	
153	**Never leave it empty.** A finding with no fix renders as a dash, and a column
154	of dashes is the reader's evidence that the report describes problems it cannot
155	help with.
156	
157	**The title carries the finding.** `Same meal shows three different times across surfaces` — not `Timestamp issue` and not `Investigation of meal timestamps`. A reader scanning only the titles should get the whole report.
158	
159	**⚑ `Locator` is not optional, even though the gate will tolerate its absence.**
160	
161	The ID is `hash(lens + flow + locator + title)`. If you omit this field the gate
162	*infers* a locator — the first `` `/path` `` in the body, else the first Evidence
163	artifact — and if that differs from what you hashed, the ID is rejected.
164	
165	Writing the field makes the two agree by construction. It also makes the ID
166	reproducible by a human, and immune to a future change in inference rules.
167	
168	> Observed 2026-09-04: a lens passed `--locator` to the script but did not write
169	> the field. The gate found `/privacy` in the finding's prose, inferred that
170	> instead, and rejected two otherwise-correct IDs. Passing `--locator` to the
171	> script does nothing on its own — **the report has to say what you hashed.**
172	
173	**`So what` is the field most often written badly.** It is not a restatement of the title and not a framework citation. *"She could not tell which time the product had actually recorded"* is a so-what; *"violates consistency heuristic A4"* is not.
174	
175	```markdown
176	---
177	
178	## Dropped for want of evidence
179	Observations that did not meet the evidence rule. **Not findings.**
180	
181	- <observation> — <what evidence was missing>
182	
183	## For other lenses
184	- <observation> — <which lens>
185	
186	## Coverage gaps
187	- <surface never opened, flow never completed, device never tested>
188	
189	## Appendices
190	- A. Persona debriefs
191	- B. Session timelines
192	- C. Screenshot index
193	```
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Rules
198	
199	**One finding = one issue.** Do not merge unrelated problems because they share a screen.
200	
201	**Dedupe across personas.** Same issue hit by three personas → one finding, `Personas hit: a, b, c`.
202	
203	**⚑ Split when severity flips.** If the same behaviour is P1 for one persona and a non-issue for another, that is **two findings**, not an average. Name the persona-specific variants (`<id>-a`, `<id>-b`) and flag the flip in the exec summary.
204	
205	> A flip usually means the product has picked a user without saying so. Averaging it away destroys the most valuable signal the method produces — and it is the failure mode a hurried analyst falls into every time.
206	
207	**Cite the exact on-page wording in quotation marks when a finding turns on
208	copy.** Two lenses quoting the same string is how the run level detects that
209	they found the same thing — see `commands/run.md` §3.6. Paraphrasing the label
210	costs that link, and costs the reader the ability to search for it.
211	
212	**Do NOT dedupe across lenses.** Each lens report stands alone and is read alone; a problem another lens also found still belongs in yours, scored on your terms. Cross-lens overlap is reconciled once, at the run level, by the orchestrator — never by you, and never by reading another lens's output.
213	
214	**Every finding carries a stable ID.** `scripts/finding_id.py --lens <lens> --flow <flow> --locator <where> --title <title>`. Not a sequence number — the ID must survive across runs so `report --since` can classify **new · persisting · resolved**. IDs cannot be retrofitted.
215	
216	**Every finding cites evidence.** No exceptions, including for findings that are obviously true. See `evidence-rules.md`.
217	
218	**The verdict is the strongest honest reading.** Not bland, not polite, not hedged. If the product is good, say so plainly; a report that cannot say anything positive is as untrustworthy as one that cannot say anything negative.
219	
220	**Never compare to competitors the user did not ask about.**
221	
222	**Never report an excluded item.** Scope exclusions from the target file are applied here, at scoring — the traversal still recorded what it saw. An excluded thing that blocked the persona still explains why they got stuck; it explains, it does not score.
223	
224	**Never report the auth wall.** Infrastructure, always.

1. **Conclusion first, everywhere.** The finding title *is* the conclusion. The exec summary opens with the verdict. A reader who stops after one line must still have the answer.
2. **Bullets, not paragraphs.** No prose blocks anywhere in a report. If a thought needs three sentences, it is three bullets — or it is two thoughts.
3. **One idea per bullet, ≤ 25 words.** Longer means it is really two bullets.
4. **Cut anything that does not change a decision.** Background, throat-clearing, "it is worth noting that", restating the framework. The reader knows why they ran this.
5. **Numbers over adjectives.** "2:41 to first value" beats "reasonably quick".

**Why this is a rule and not a preference:** a lens can produce twenty findings, and a run can carry seven lenses. Prose does not survive that volume — it is skimmed, then skipped, then the report goes unread and the run was wasted. Pyramid structure is what lets a reader stop at any depth and still be correctly informed.

**What concision must never cost:** evidence citations, repro steps, or the severity. Compress the *reasoning*, never the *proof*. A finding stripped of its evidence is not concise, it is unsupported — see `evidence-rules.md`.

---

## Why the exec summary leads with a verdict

The one-sentence verdict and the top-3 are the only things standing between the user and a great deal of unread output. **Phase-2 gate check 6 enforces this mechanically** — a report whose first non-heading block is not a single sentence fails the gate.

Write the verdict first, before the findings. If you cannot state the verdict in one sentence, you have not finished analysing.

---

**Length: about one page.** Soft target, not a gate — but every line past it should have earned its place.

```markdown
# <Product> — <lens> — Run <YYYY-MM-DD> (<run-id>)

<ONE SENTENCE. The strongest honest reading of the evidence. No hedging,
no "it depends", no list. This is the line someone repeats in a meeting.>

## Top 3
1. **[P0] <Title>** — <one line: the cost, not the description> (<personas>)
2. **[P1] <Title>** — <one line> (<personas>)
3. **[P1] <Title>** — <one line> (<personas>)

## Score
- **Score:** <N>/10 — <one line saying what drove it, in the reader's terms>

## Limits on this read
- **Personas:** <list> — ⚠ INFERRED (generic) | researched (supplied)
- **Not reached:** <surfaces, flows — or "none">
- **Excluded:** <scope exclusions, verbatim — auth wall always>
- **Models:** traversal `<model>` · scoring `<model>`

## Numbers
| Persona | TTFV | Reading | Self-explanatory | Promise match |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <name> | <MM:SS> | healthy / at risk / not reached | Pass/Partial/Fail | Pass/Partial/Fail |

## Severity flips
<One line per behaviour scoring differently across personas. "None" if none —
and if only one persona ran, say that instead: a flip could not be observed.>

## Next action
<One line.>
```

### ⚑ The score

**You assign it, because you are the only one who read the evidence.** The run
report renders every lens's score in one table with an overall figure, so this
number is read by the client beside the other checks — a lens that scores
generously, or harshly, distorts every other lens's number by comparison.

- **10** — nothing to fix that a reasonable reviewer would raise.
- **8–9** — works; the findings are polish.
- **6–7** — works, with friction a real user would notice and complain about.
- **4–5** — a user gets through, but a meaningful share would give up or distrust it.
- **2–3** — the job this check covers mostly fails.
- **0–1** — unusable on this dimension.

**Gate check 7 refuses a score its own severities contradict** — above 5/10
carrying a P0, above 7/10 carrying a P1, above 9/10 carrying a P2. The ceiling
is loose on purpose: it stops a number nobody could defend, it does not
second-guess a judgement inside the band — and it is a ceiling, not a target.
**Score from what the personas did, then check the ceiling; never start from
the ceiling and subtract.** Every persona reached value and would return is a
6–7 even with a P1 and a dozen P2s; the 4–5 band means someone actually gave
up. The bands, with what each looks like, are in `lens-output-contract.md`.
Score the dimension, not the count of findings — eleven P3s is a tidy 8, not
a 3.

by `render_report.py`, so the cover and the table cannot disagree.

```markdown
- Framework: <the lens's framework, one line>

- Personas: <generic — INFERRED | supplied — researched>
- Scoring model: <model>
- Every finding cites an artifact; unsupported observations dropped, listed at the end

---

> **⚑ This block is machine-parsed.** `check_report.py` reads it field by field
> and fails closed — a field it cannot find is treated as absent, and an absent
> `Flow` silently changes the finding's ID. **Keep every field on its own

> field's value is fine and expected (several artifacts on one Evidence line);

>
> **The `<finding-id>` is computed, never composed** — see the lens agent's

> hash exactly the `flow`, `locator` and `title` strings you wrote.

- **So what:** <ONE line. What this costs this persona. The reason to fix it.>
- **Framework tags:** <A?, B-G?, C-? — per the lens>

  - <bullet>

  2. …
```

as an instruction someone could hand to a developer or a copywriter — name the
surface and the change. *"Delete the eyebrow, and add a self-serve link from
that section to /restaurants"* is a fix; *"reconsider the framing"* is not.

of dashes is the reader's evidence that the report describes problems it cannot
help with.

The ID is `hash(lens + flow + locator + title)`. If you omit this field the gate
*infers* a locator — the first `` `/path` `` in the body, else the first Evidence
artifact — and if that differs from what you hashed, the ID is rejected.

Writing the field makes the two agree by construction. It also makes the ID
reproducible by a human, and immune to a future change in inference rules.

> the field. The gate found `/privacy` in the finding's prose, inferred that
> instead, and rejected two otherwise-correct IDs. Passing `--locator` to the
> script does nothing on its own — **the report has to say what you hashed.**

```markdown
Observations that did not meet the evidence rule. **Not findings.**

- <observation> — <what evidence was missing>

## For other lenses
- <observation> — <which lens>

## Coverage gaps
- <surface never opened, flow never completed, device never tested>

## Appendices
- A. Persona debriefs
- B. Session timelines
- C. Screenshot index
```

---

## Rules

**One finding = one issue.** Do not merge unrelated problems because they share a screen.

**Dedupe across personas.** Same issue hit by three personas → one finding, `Personas hit: a, b, c`.

**⚑ Split when severity flips.** If the same behaviour is P1 for one persona and a non-issue for another, that is **two findings**, not an average. Name the persona-specific variants (`<id>-a`, `<id>-b`) and flag the flip in the exec summary.

> A flip usually means the product has picked a user without saying so. Averaging it away destroys the most valuable signal the method produces — and it is the failure mode a hurried analyst falls into every time.

**Cite the exact on-page wording in quotation marks when a finding turns on
copy.** Two lenses quoting the same string is how the run level detects that
they found the same thing — see `commands/run.md` §3.6. Paraphrasing the label
costs that link, and costs the reader the ability to search for it.

**Do NOT dedupe across lenses.** Each lens report stands alone and is read alone; a problem another lens also found still belongs in yours, scored on your terms. Cross-lens overlap is reconciled once, at the run level, by the orchestrator — never by you, and never by reading another lens's output.

**Every finding carries a stable ID.** `scripts/finding_id.py --lens <lens> --flow <flow> --locator <where> --title <title>`. Not a sequence number — the ID must survive across runs so `report --since` can classify **new · persisting · resolved**. IDs cannot be retrofitted.

**Every finding cites evidence.** No exceptions, including for findings that are obviously true. See `evidence-rules.md`.

**The verdict is the strongest honest reading.** Not bland, not polite, not hedged. If the product is good, say so plainly; a report that cannot say anything positive is as untrustworthy as one that cannot say anything negative.

**Never compare to competitors the user did not ask about.**

**Never report an excluded item.** Scope exclusions from the target file are applied here, at scoring — the traversal still recorded what it saw. An excluded thing that blocked the persona still explains why they got stuck; it explains, it does not score.

**Never report the auth wall.** Infrastructure, always.

# Nimbus Notes — Website assessment — 8 September 2026

## What this is

- Nimbus Notes is a note-taking app: notes are kept on the device first and synced between a laptop and a phone, exportable as a folder of Markdown files, with data held in the EU (Frankfurt) by default.

- Two stand-in buyers were given a goal and turned loose on the real site in a real browser, with everything they saw, clicked and said recorded: one on a 1440×900 desktop for 6 minutes 30, one on an iPhone 13 for 2 minutes 50.

- Both buyers were constructed for this assessment, not recruited from real customers.

## Objectives

| 3 | P2 | The one explaining sentence reads "A bi-directional sync graph with a zero-knowledge vault" | The desktop buyer could not define either term and stopped trying at 18 seconds; the sentence meant to explain the product explains nothing | Copy change |
| 4 | P2 | "Features" is second in the navigation on every page and returns a 404 | A buyer who cannot understand the product from the home page goes here for the answer and gets an error instead | Build |
| 5 | P2 | No page says who the product is for; the only audience wording — "For individuals." / "For growing teams." — sits on the pricing cards | A buyer evaluating for a team cannot tell whether this is a personal tool, so cannot tell whether to keep reading | Copy change |

|---|---|

| Who is it for? | Not answered on any page the buyers read. The only audience wording is on the pricing cards, one click away |
| Can I see it working? | Not answered. The desktop buyer clicked "See it in action" twice at 00:40, the phone buyer tapped it at 02:20; nothing happened either time |
| What does it cost? | Not answered. Three plans, all "Contact sales", no figures; the desktop buyer gave up at 02:30 and declined the seven-field form behind it |
| Who is behind this company? | Answered, on About: named founder, Bristol address, company number, eight people. The phone buyer found it at 01:30 |

|---|---|---|---|

| evaluator | 00:18 | "'bi-directional sync graph', 'zero-knowledge vault' — I don't know what either means." | findings-raw.json t=00:18 · Top 5 #3 |
| evaluator | 00:40 | "Clicked "See it in action". Nothing happened. The page didn't move. Clicked again. Still nothing." | session.log:12 · Top 5 #2 |
| sceptic | 02:20 | "Back to the home page. I want to see it "remember" something. The button does nothing when I tap it." | session.log:13 · Top 5 #2 |
| evaluator | 03:30 | "Features in the nav goes to a 404." | findings-raw.json t=03:30 · 04-features-404.png · Top 5 #4 |
| sceptic | debrief Q2 | "The page doesn't say. Possibly me." | persona-debrief.md Q2 · Top 5 #5 |
| evaluator | 03:50 | "OK — a real company, eight people, founded 2023 by Priya Raman, Bristol, a company number. That's the first thing on this site that felt like a real business." | session.log:24 · 05-about.png |

| Check | Question it answers |
|---|---|

## How to read these findings

| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|

| 🟠 **P1** | They get through, but would not become a customer |
| 🟡 **P2** | Noticeable friction; erodes value over time |
| ⚪ **P3** | Polish. Worth fixing, changes nothing on its own |

- Both buyers were constructed, not recruited: their reactions are a reasoned stand-in for real visitors, not customer research.

- The phone buyer never opened Pricing, so pricing comprehension on a small screen is untested.
